scope.description: Whether a client membership change issued to a node whose configuration is the reconstructed one commits with support that is not a majority of the configuration it replaces, and whether the peers it demotes adopt it. Nineteen in-process cases: the seventeen previously exercised restart shapes plus a client_change_on_reconstruction case run with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and disabled. In that case a three-voter cluster is collapsed to one voter, snapshotted, made three voters again, every instance is stopped, and only the former leader is restarted together with a fresh empty fourth instance; a client AddVoter for that instance is issued with prevIndex 0, and the two demoted peers are then restarted with the flag disabled.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transports and the in-memory commit-tracking log store from the captured package; the fresh instance has its own empty log, stable and snapshot stores and is connected to the restarted leader in both directions, and the returning peers are reconnected likewise.
The two peers of the committed configuration are deliberately kept down while the change is issued, so the leader cannot reach them and any commit must rest on itself and the fresh instance.
The client change is the package's own AddVoter with prevIndex 0, as the package's AddPeer and RemovePeer helpers also use.

The change wait is 400 ms and the observation of the returning peers a further 400 ms; the returning peers are restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs disabled so their own configuration comes from their logs.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, membership changes with a nonzero prevIndex, concurrent client changes, and any claim about leadership among disjoint configurations after a partition.

basis.prefix: The new case builds a three-peer cluster with MakeClusterCustom(MakeClusterOpts{Peers: 3, Bootstrap: true, CommitTrackingLogs: true, Conf: inmemConfig with TrailingLogs 10 and RestoreCommittedLogs set per case}), demotes both non-leader peers, applies 100 commands, takes leader.Snapshot(), promotes both peers back and applies ten more entries, reads the last configuration entry and emits a change_inputs CA_EVENT, then shuts down every instance. It restarts only the former leader over its own stores with the case flag, starts one fresh empty instance (own stores, its own MockFSM, connected to the leader in both directions), waits for the leader, records its reconstructed voter count, issues AddVoter for the fresh instance with prevIndex 0 and records the outcome, then rebuilds the two demoted peers with the flag disabled, reconnects them to the leader and waits. It emits a change_result CA_EVENT with the leader's reconstructed and replaced voter counts and server sets, the change outcome and error, whether the new member holds a vote and whether it was in the replaced configuration, the fresh instance's reconstructed voter count, and how many demoted peers adopted the rewritten configuration and how many of them ended with a vote.
basis.responsibility: The leader computes a client membership change from configurations.latest and rebuilds its commitment from the resulting configuration, so whether a change commits with the replaced configuration's support is decided by that configuration rather than by the one recorded in the leader's log.

comparisons.description: Client-change case with the flag enabled: a node leading on a reconstructed configuration is not expected to commit a membership change that replaces the committed configuration with support that is not its majority.
Control: with the flag disabled the same node cannot be leader with the other members down, so no membership change commits.
Client-change case with the flag enabled: whether both peers that held votes in the replaced configuration ended up adopting the rewritten configuration in which they hold none.
Client-change case with the flag enabled: records that the member added by the change is not part of the configuration the change replaced.

before.description: Whether a peer whose reconstruction still grants it a vote, but whose committed configuration does not, can campaign on its own and acquire leadership with support from a peer that also reconstructs a configuration. Seventeen in-process cases: the fifteen previously exercised restart shapes plus a stale_campaign_wins case run with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and disabled. In that case one peer snapshots itself while still a voter, its vote is removed in the committed configuration, all instances are stopped, and only that peer and one other are restarted while the former leader stays down.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transports and the in-memory commit-tracking log store from the captured package; both rebuilt instances are reconnected to each other in both directions.
The former leader is deliberately left down so that neither rebuilt instance knows a leader and the known-leader rejection cannot mask the vote path.

The peer that campaigns holds a snapshot of the configuration in which it was still a voter and a tracked commit index that covers the configuration entry removing its vote, which is what the flag-enabled reconstruction reads instead.

The other instance holds no snapshot of its own, so its flag-enabled reconstruction is empty; the campaign is entirely produced by the target's own state machine and delivered over the real transport.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, pre-vote-only campaigns without a following real election, membership changes during the window, and any claim about what a full restored cluster would decide afterwards.

prefix.before: The new case builds a three-peer cluster with MakeClusterCustom(MakeClusterOpts{Peers: 3, Bootstrap: true, CommitTrackingLogs: true, Conf: inmemConfig with TrailingLogs 10 and RestoreCommittedLogs set per case}), applies 20 commands, has one non-leader peer take its own snapshot through the public API while it is still a voter, records that snapshot's configuration index and voter count, then calls leader.DemoteVoter for that peer and applies ten more entries. It reads the peer's own log configuration entry, voter count, member and vote status and tracked commit index and emits a campaign_inputs CA_EVENT, stops every instance, rebuilds only that peer and the third peer over their own stores with the case flag, reconnects them to each other, registers an observer on the third peer for incoming pre-vote and vote requests, waits up to 1500 ms for the campaigning peer to become leader, and emits a campaign_result CA_EVENT with both peers' reconstructed voter counts, the peer's vote status in its own committed configuration, whether it became leader, its final state and how many pre-vote and vote requests the third peer received.

responsibility.before: runFollower and runCandidate decide whether the node campaigns and how many grants it needs, and requestVote on the answering peer decides whether to grant, so a reconstructed configuration that grants the node a vote it does not have lets leadership be acquired with support the committed configuration does not sanction.

before.description: Campaign case with the flag enabled: a peer that holds no vote in the configuration recorded in its own log is not expected to acquire leadership.
Control: with the flag disabled the same peer reconstructs the committed configuration, holds no vote there and does not campaign.
Campaign case with the flag enabled: whether the campaigning peer's real vote request reached the other instance in this execution.

revision_reason: Adds the client_change_on_reconstruction case with its flag-disabled control, in which a client membership change is issued to a node leading on a reconstructed configuration while the peers of the committed configuration are down, and those peers are then restarted to observe whether they adopt the rewritten configuration. Replaces the comparison set with the commit predicate, its control and the adoption and membership premises.
